examples.solution_text:
The brace is the hypotenuse.
$\begin{aligned}d&=\sqrt{1.6^{2}+1.2^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{4}\\&=2\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

The ladder is the hypotenuse; the height is a shorter side.
$\begin{aligned}h&=\sqrt{6^{2}-2^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{32}\\&\approx5.66\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: The numbers $28$, $45$ and $c$ form a Pythagorean triad, where $c$ is the largest number. Find $c$.

examples.solution_text:
The perpendicular height bisects the base, making two right-angled triangles. Each has base $14\div2=7\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned}h&=\sqrt{14^{2}-7^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{147}\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

Let the width be $x\text{ cm}$, so the length is $2x\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned}x^{2}+(2x)^{2}&=12^{2}\\5x^{2}&=144\\x^{2}&=28.8\\x&=\sqrt{28.8}\end{aligned}$
The width is $\sqrt{28.8}\text{ cm}\approx5.37\text{ cm}$ and the length is $2\sqrt{28.8}\text{ cm}\approx10.73\text{ cm}$.

examples.question_text: Two sides of a right-angled triangle measure $12\text{ cm}$ and $16\text{ cm}$. Find both possible lengths of the third side. Round to $2$ decimal places where required.
examples.solution_text:
If both given sides are shorter sides, the third side is the hypotenuse.
$\begin{aligned}x&=\sqrt{12^{2}+16^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{400}\\&=20\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
If $16\text{ cm}$ is the hypotenuse, the third side is a shorter side.
$\begin{aligned}x&=\sqrt{16^{2}-12^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{112}\\&\approx10.58\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
The two possible lengths are $20\text{ cm}$ and approximately $10.58\text{ cm}$.

examples.derivation: 1.6² + 1.2² = 2.56 + 1.44 = 4; d = √4 = 2 m. The rectangle's diagonal is the hypotenuse. Matches source Development Q5, lines 792–800 and image51.
h² = 6² − 2² = 32; h = √32 = 5.656854… m, rounding to 5.66 m. The ladder is opposite the marked right angle. Matches source Development Q4, lines 944–950 and image59.

Height difference = 5.9 − 3.5 = 2.4 m; s² = 7² + 2.4² = 54.76; s = 7.4 m. The solution diagram correctly isolates the right-angled triangle and adds the derived height only in the solution. Matches lines 1214–1223 and image89.
c² = 28² + 45² = 784 + 2025 = 2809 = 53²; c = 53. All three members are whole numbers and c is largest. A diagram is unnecessary. Matches lines 1225–1228.

The perpendicular height bisects the 14 cm base into 7 cm halves. h² = 14² − 7² = 147; h = √147 cm. The diagram preserves the full base given without exposing the derived half-base answer. Matches Mastery Q13a, lines 1296–1300.

x² + (2x)² = 144 gives 5x² = 144 and x² = 28.8. Positive width √28.8 = 5.366563… cm; length 2√28.8 = 10.733126… cm. Dimensions round to 5.37 cm by 10.73 cm. The diagram shows the stated ratio and diagonal consistently. Matches lines 1278–1294.

If both given sides are legs, x = √(144 + 256) = 20 cm. If 16 cm is the hypotenuse, x = √(256 − 144) = √112 = 10.583005… cm, rounding to 10.58 cm. The 12 cm side cannot be the hypotenuse because 16 cm is longer. A fixed diagram is unnecessary for these two cases. Matches lines 1240–1252.
